title: The Disappearance of Childhood
description: The Disappearance of Childhood is an ongoing series of work inspired by Neil Postman's book of the same title. Beginning with his observation that media technologies reshape the boundary between childhood and adulthood, the series extends this inquiry into the contemporary condition. As social media, artificial intelligence, digital entertainment, and algorithmic systems increasingly mediate everyday life, the work examines how childhood continues to be constructed, negotiated, and transformed. Rather than treating childhood as a natural state, the series considers it a cultural condition whose boundaries are constantly being redefined.

title: Gardening
description: Gardening continues my exploration of the relationship between childhood and cultivation. I approach gardening as a process of nurturing, shaping, and pruning, proposing that childhood is similarly constructed through the ongoing influence of family, education, media, and social norms rather than existing as a natural state. Centering on the Garden Gnome—a figure suspended between fairy tale, domestic ornament, and commodity—the series places these characters within absurd, playful narratives to imagine alternative possibilities for childhood and question the systems through which it is continually cultivated.

title: Welcome to Adulthood
displayTitle: Welcome to Adulthood, I hope you like ...
description: This series examines educational toys as technologies of childhood. By transforming “A is for Apple” into “A is for Addiction,” the work shifts a familiar learning device into a metaphor for the invisible systems through which discipline, desire, and consumer culture are introduced at an early age. Childhood is approached not as a natural state, but as a socially constructed concept.
